title: The Cover of the Green Zone
premise: Jude Almeida, a veteran interpreter for a doomed peace delegation in the contested border city of Verano, receives a burner phone containing recordings that prove a massacre seven years ago was orchestrated by the very officials now brokering peace. The voice on the line belongs to Tomas, Jude's presumed-dead brother and former militia informant, who is alive, hunted, and willing to trade the evidence only if Jude smuggles it past three governments' intelligence services and an assassin codenamed Ferro who has already killed two couriers. As the delegation collapses around them, Jude must choose between the loyalty that kept them invisible and the truth that will burn every protection they have. In the end, Jude delivers the recordings not to any government but to the victims' families themselves, exposing the peace process at the cost of Tomas's life and their own safe anonymity.
about_author: Sable Joubert is a former humanitarian field officer who spent six years in post-conflict zones before turning to fiction full-time. They write from a converted fishing cottage on the Atlantic coast, drawing on the moral gray zones they witnessed firsthand.

chapters.title: The Language of Small Surrenders
chapters.summary: POV Jude. On the eve of the Verano peace summit, Jude interprets a preliminary meeting and quietly mistranslates one word to defuse a flare-up, showing how they survive by bending language. The emotional beat is weary competence masking dread as rumors of leaks circulate through the delegation.

chapters.title: A Phone That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Finding a burner phone taped beneath their hotel room's loose floorboard, Jude answers a call and hears Tomas's voice—impossible, since Tomas died seven years ago in the Kestrel Valley massacre. The beat is vertigo: grief cracking open into suspicion that everything Jude believed about that night was staged.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, POV Jude. We learn how Jude came to Verano, how Tomas worked as a militia informant, and how his body was never recovered—only his dog tags mailed anonymously. The beat is tender, establishing the sibling bond and the guilt Jude has carried like a second passport.

chapters.title: Ferro
chapters.summary: POV antagonist. The assassin Ferro reviews photographs of two dead couriers in another city and crosses names off a list until only one remains: an interpreter named Almeida. Cold, procedural, almost gentle in tone—the beat is quiet menace, letting readers know the clock has started.

chapters.title: Proof of Life
chapters.summary: POV Jude. A second call gives coordinates to a locker; inside are recordings implicating Deputy Minister Corvane in ordering the Kestrel Valley massacre. Tomas's instructions are terse: get this out or more people die. The beat is terrified resolve as Jude realizes invisibility was always someone else's arrangement.

chapters.title: The Delegation Eats Its Own
chapters.summary: POV Jude. At the summit's opening plenary, Jude notices Corvane watching them across the hall, and their section chief, Ilse Brandt, warns them off 'old ghosts.' The beat is paranoia tightening: Jude can no longer tell which colleagues are protectors and which are watchers.

chapters.title: What Ilse Knows
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Brandt. The chief of delegation confronts her own complicity—she signed the security memo that erased Tomas from official records years ago. Torn between career and conscience, she decides to watch Jude rather than report them. The beat is corrosive self-justification beginning to fail.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV rotating brief sections. Intelligence officers from each of the three governments receive fragments of the same warning about a leak tied to Kestrel Valley, and each decides to control it rather than expose it. The beat is institutional cynicism—the truth is now a liability everyone wants to own.

chapters.title: The Rooftop in the Rain
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Following Tomas's instructions, Jude waits on a rooftop and finally sees him—alive, scarred, half a stranger. Their reunion is interrupted by a tail Jude barely loses. The beat is joy curdling into fear: Tomas is not the brother who left, and he is leading something dangerous.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Currency
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Through his eyes we learn he survived by becoming an asset for a third party—mercenaries turned brokers—who now want the recordings released to collapse the summit for profit. The beat is tragic ambiguity: Tomas loves Jude but has been using them all along.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Transporting copies of the recordings hidden in translation notes, Jude is stopped at a checkpoint where a young soldier recognizes the Kestrel Valley insignia—and lets them pass, whispering that his sister died there. The beat is unexpected solidarity: the truth has allies in low places.

chapters.title: Ilse Makes Her Choice
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Discovering Jude's copies, Ilse instead of reporting them burns her own copy of the old memo and offers Jude one warning: Ferro is already in the city. The beat is redemption arriving late and imperfectly, costing Ilse her last illusions about the process she served.

chapters.title: The Interrogation Room
chapters.summary: POV Jude. Detained briefly by the second government's security service, Jude survives interrogation by translating for their own interrogator and planting doubt between the three services. The beat is Jude's transformation—from instrument to operator, using language as a weapon instead of a shield.

chapters.title: What the Recordings Say
chapters.summary: POV Jude, listening alone at night. Full playback reveals Corvane's voice, but also Tomas's—present at the massacre, coerced into silence, his 'death' part of the cover-up. The beat is devastation: the truth indicts the person Jude loves most, forcing loyalty and truth into open war.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV alternating Jude/Tomas. Jude demands Tomas testify publicly; Tomas refuses, arguing release through the mercenary brokers saves lives faster. Their argument becomes a reckoning over seven years of secrets. The beat is heartbreak—both are right, and both know it cannot stay that way.

chapters.title: Ferro Closes In
chapters.summary: POV Ferro, then Jude. Ferro traces the rooftop meeting and hits the safehouse minutes after Jude leaves; Tomas escapes wounded. Ferro, reviewing the file, hesitates for the first time—he grew up near Kestrel Valley. The beat is the assassin's certainty developing a hairline fracture.

chapters.title: The Summit Fractures
chapters.summary: POV Jude. With the delegation collapsing mid-session, Jude makes a move no one expects: they begin interpreting the closing statements while feeding fragments of the recordings' transcript into the official record under cover of translation. The beat is audacious risk—the truth entering the machine through its own mouthpiece.

chapters.title: Corvane's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. The deputy minister moves to have Jude discredited as unstable, producing forged psychiatric records, and orders Ferro to finish the job before the final session. The beat is cold power flexing—but Corvane underestimates how many small people Jude has quietly won over.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Jude. On the summit's final morning, Jude walks the corridor to the plenary knowing Ferro is somewhere ahead. Ilse stalls security; the checkpoint soldier's testimony arrives via a journalist. The beat is sustained dread breaking into courage—Jude stops hiding behind words and steps into the light.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Jude, climax. Before delegates and cameras, Jude abandons interpretation and speaks in their own voice, playing the recordings as Ferro enters the hall—then lowers his weapon, refusing the order, and instead confirms the massacre aloud. The beat is cathartic rupture: justice spoken outside every law in the room.

chapters.title: The Price of the Truth
chapters.summary: POV Jude. In the chaos, Tomas sacrifices himself covering Jude's escape from Corvane's remaining loyalists, dying in Jude's arms with the dog tags finally returned. Corvane is arrested by his own government to contain the damage. The beat is grief braided with vindication—truth delivered, at the cost of everything personal.

chapters.title: After the Green Zone
chapters.summary: POV Jude, epilogue. Months later, Jude testifies before an international commission, no longer an interpreter but a witness, while the Kestrel Valley families receive the full archive. Leaving Verano, Jude mails the burner phone—now silent—to no one, keeping only Tomas's tags. The beat is hard-won peace: visible at last, and unafraid.
